mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a consistent four-week recovery trend (-31.6 to -12.1), reflecting an ongoing reopening trajectory. This underlying momentum in retail footfall is expected to persist mechanically into the next four weeks absent any new shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved every week for 4 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days, breaking the observed momentum.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has been recovering steadily (-46.4 to -26.1). Once TRANSIT crosses a recovery threshold of -30, it signals enough commuter and shopper ridership returning to drive a corresponding rise in RETAIL_REC within two weeks as people resume in-person shopping trips.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -26.1 at t-0w, crossing above -30 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise or declines in the two weeks following TRANSIT crossing above -30.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved from -42.4 to -25.6 over four weeks, consistent with a policy-driven easing of work-from-home mandates. Under an active reopening regime, continued WORKPLACES recovery will lift associated retail and recreation visits near workplaces over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved monotonically over the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise despite WORKPLACES continuing to improve, or regime shifts to renewed restrictions and RETAIL_REC still rises.

mechanism_narrative: When both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise together week-on-week, their combined effect compounds commuter-driven retail visits beyond what either series alone would predict, producing an outsized rise in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks via joint restoration of daily routines.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved each of the last 3 weeks simultaneously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rise is no larger than predicted by either single-series model, or RETAIL_REC falls despite joint WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increases.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has surged to 65.0, indicating strong seasonal preference for outdoor leisure. When PARKS exceeds 60, substitution effects pull discretionary leisure time away from indoor retail and recreation venues, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds 60 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached 65.0 at t-0w, exceeding 60 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise in the week following PARKS exceeding 60, showing no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 5.1 to 1.4, indicating people are spending less time at home. This reduction in home-centric behavior directly frees time and propensity for out-of-home shopping and recreation trips, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 5.1 to 1.4 over the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next two weeks despite continued decline in RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility, typically the least restriction-sensitive category, has improved from -24.4 to -9.4, signaling broad policy-driven normalization of essential and non-essential mobility alike. Under an active policy-easing regime, this normalization pattern implies RETAIL_REC will continue converging toward baseline over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved monotonically each week for 4 weeks
regime_hint: policy-easing regime with lifted mobility restrictions
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stagnates or declines while GROCERY_PHARM continues improving, or regime reverts to tightened restrictions yet RETAIL_REC still rises.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT recovers faster than WORKPLACES (the gap between their weekly improvements widens beyond 10 points), it suggests transit capacity is being used for non-commute discretionary travel already saturating available retail capacity, causing a short-term pullback in RETAIL_REC the following week due to crowding or saturation effects.
candidate_trigger: weekly improvement in TRANSIT exceeds weekly improvement in WORKPLACES by more than 10 points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved by 7.0 points and WORKPLACES by 2.0 points between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise in the week following a TRANSIT-WORKPLACES divergence exceeding 10 points, contradicting the predicted pullback.
